content:
iPadOS and macOS were two very different software platforms in the past. But especially since iPadOS 26, the two have become increasingly similar. And this year the situation is even more obvious, with iPadOS 27 adding three features that make the iPad closer to the Mac than ever before.

#1: Status bar displays app name

I have been using an M5 iPad Pro connected to a Magic Keyboard long-term. For keyboard users, the iPad has long had a problem, namely the lack of a clear "active app" indicator.

If there is only one app on the screen, there is no such problem. But if multiple apps are visible at the same time, keyboard shortcuts become very difficult to handle. I cannot count how many times I thought a certain shortcut would trigger inside one app, only to find it actually acted on another app.

Mac solved this problem a long time ago by putting the name of the active app in the upper left corner of the screen. Now iPadOS 27 does the same thing.

iPadOS 27 users will see the name of the active app in the status bar, located next to status bar elements like the time and date. Although this change is very small, it is very welcome and makes the experience of using an iPad with a keyboard much more pleasant.

#2: Always-visible menu bar

Another welcome iPadOS 27 change is the option to always display the menu bar.

Apple brought the menu bar to the iPad for the first time last year. But unlike the Mac, the menu bar in iPadOS 26 only appeared when the user actively summoned it.

In iPadOS 27, a new toggle option has been added under "Multitasking & Gestures" in the Settings app, labelled: "Automatically show and hide menu bar".

If you turn this toggle off, the menu bar will remain displayed at all times. I have been using this mode during the iPadOS beta, and it is one of my favourite changes this year.

#3: Mac-level speed for everyday operations

Although I really like my iPad and am very grateful for its new capabilities in iPadOS 26 and 27, I sometimes get annoyed by some basic operations being too slow. For example, earlier this year I wrote: "Right-clicking in iPadOS often feels sluggish and laggy, but on the Mac it responds instantly."

Thanks to Apple's aggressive bug fixes this year, I am happy to say that iPadOS 27 has improved the speed of these kinds of everyday operations.

Apple says opening context menus with a mouse is faster, and I can definitely feel it. Browsing files and transferring them to an external hard drive is now "up to 5 times faster", and Apple says this speed is now as fast as Finder on the Mac. App launch responsiveness is more agile, and window management operations like closing, switching, or dragging windows have also sped up.

There are still some areas where the Mac is faster and the iPad seems a bit slow. But overall, the speed improvements in iPadOS 27 are a big step in the right direction.

What are your favourite new features and changes in iPadOS 27? Feel free to let us know in the comments section.
